finding.claim: The /rss endpoint passes the user-supplied `u` query parameter straight to URI.open and returns the first 400 bytes of the response. An attacker can make the server fetch arbitrary URLs, including internal services and cloud metadata endpoints such as http://169.254.169.254/. Because the body is returned, this is a full-read SSRF.

trace.note: params[:u] is passed unchanged to URI.open, which performs the outbound HTTP/HTTPS/FTP request
the first 400 bytes of the fetched body are returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host or IP allowlist, and no private-range or DNS-rebinding checks. TRUSTED is not applied on this route. The only limit is truncating the response to 400 bytes.

verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes the unauthenticated query param params[:u] directly to URI.open(...).read with no validation, and app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes. The TRUSTED check at app.rb:14 applies only to /trusted, not to /rss.
